newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets rise.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its international reserves as of May 9 were $21.773 billion, compared to $21.446 billion on May 2.
The central bank said that its net international assets as of the same date rose to $12.715 billion from $12.383 billion the week before.
The central bank said the increase of $332 million in net international assets during the period was due to:
--Net purchases of foreign currency from the federal government worth $177 million.
--Net income from operations by the state oil company Pemex worth $157 million.
--Net payment to the International Monetary Fund for $116 million.

--A net gain of $114 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said that between May 2 and May 9 the monetary base fell 2.476 billion pesos due to a fall in the seasonal demand of bills and coins.
In the same period, the government's balance at the central bank rose 1.988 billion pesos, due to the net sale of foreign exchange to Banco de Mexico.

The bank said it undertook monetary regulation operations for a total of 2.612 billion pesos in the same time frame in order to meet a greater demand for bills and coins as well as other more minor effects.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
May 2 May 9
International Reserves
U.S. Dollars $21.446 bln $21.773 bln
Monetary Base 79.222 76.746
Net International Assets*
U.S. Dollars $12.383 bln $12.715 bln
Net Domestic Credit -18.746 -23.744
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
((--David Luhnow, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7902))
